## Data

```{r}
#| label: load-pkgs
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data-1

super_bowl_data_1 <- read.csv("data/super-bowl-dataset-1.csv", col.names = c( "index", "game", "date", "winning_team", "winning_team_points", "winning_team_conference", "score", "losing_team", "losing_team_points", "losing_team_conference", "venue", "city", "attendance", "network", "avg_us_viewers", "rating", "share", "cost_per_30_sec_ad", "notes"))

```

```{r}
#| label: tidying-dataset-1

super_bowl_data_1 <- super_bowl_data_1 |>
  mutate(date = mdy(date)) |> 
  select(-index, -winning_team_conference, -losing_team_conference, -venue, -city, -notes) |> 
  mutate(avg_us_viewers = as.numeric(avg_us_viewers))

```

```{r}
#| label: plot-1

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = date, y = avg_us_viewers)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "5 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-06, suffix = " mil")) +
  labs(
    title = "Average U.S Television Viewers over Time",
    caption = "",
    x = "Date of Super Bowl",
    y = "Average U.S Television Viewers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
#| label: plot-2

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = date, y = cost_per_30_sec_ad)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Cost of 30 second Advertisement by Year",
    caption = "",
    x = "Super Bowl Year",
    y = "Cost of 30 second Advertisement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
#| label: plot-3

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = (winning_team_points - losing_team_points), y = cost_per_30_sec_ad, color = network)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Cost of 30 second Advertisement by Point Differential across Networks",
    caption = "",
    x = "Point Differential",
    y = "Cost of 30 second Advertisement",
    color = "Network"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 1e-06, suffix = " mil")) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#| label: plot-4

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = avg_us_viewers, y = cost_per_30_sec_ad, color = network)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Cost of a 30 second Ad based on Average U.S Viewers by Network",
    caption = "",
    x = "Average U.S Viewers (in millions)",
    y = "Cost of 30 second Advertisement (in millions of $)",
    color = "Network"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-06)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 1e-06)) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#| label: plot-5

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = (winning_team_points + losing_team_points), y = (winning_team_points - losing_team_points))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    caption = "",
    x = "Total Points",
    y = "Point Difference"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#| label: calculating-correlation-1

super_bowl_data_1 |>
  mutate(year = year((date))) |>
  summarise(
    r = cor(year, cost_per_30_sec_ad),
    r2 = r^2,
    sx = sd(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    sy = sd(cost_per_30_sec_ad, na.rm = TRUE),
    b1 = r * sy/ sx
  )
```


```{r}
#| label: calculating-correlation-2

super_bowl_data_1 |> 
  summarize(
    r = cor((winning_team_points + losing_team_points), (winning_team_points - losing_team_points)),
    r2 = r ^ 2,
    sx = sd((winning_team_points + losing_team_points), na.rm = TRUE),
    sy = sd((winning_team_points - losing_team_points), na.rm = TRUE),
    b1 = r * sy / sx
)

```

## Analysis
**Hypothesis 1**


**Hypothesis 2**
The second hypothesis guiding this project was that there would be no relationship between margin of victory and total points scored with our H₁ being the inverse, yielding a significant relationship. To investigate this, Plot 4 displays a scatterplot of total points scored on the x-axis and margin of victory (point differential) on the y-axis, with both a linear fit line overlaid for comparison. At first glance, Plot 4 reveals no clear or consistent pattern between the two variables. The points on the graph depart noticeably from the linear fit, suggesting that a straight-line model is not an appropriate characterization of the relationship, and that any association present is non-linear and inconsistent across the range of values.
Our summary statistics support this visual interpretation. The correlation coefficient (R = 0.280) indicates a weak positive association between margin of victory and total points scored. Additionally, the coefficient of determination (R² = 0.078) reveals that margin of victory accounts for only approximately 8% of the variance in total points scored, meaning the vast majority of scoring variation is explained by other factors entirely.
